$Comment: A station is an ordered list of self-contained ACTIONS; this one has a single action, Mill, and everything about how milling runs is inside it. Nothing here is inherited from anywhere else in the file. Icon intentionally omitted: the engine already falls back to the anchor block's own BlockType id at engage time when Identity.Icon is absent, and this jar's own default Sawmill block shares the same id (RPG_Station_Sawmill, filename = item id), so the summary-HUD crest shows the station's own block icon with zero duplicated id to drift. Block.Exclusive true is a property of the placed block (one worker at a time), never of the job. Tool is the ONE gate for this action - a hatchet family match plus the Woods gather route - checked at engage and re-checked every heartbeat; the per-cycle durability drain rides in the same group because wear is a tool concern. Recipe authors only FromCrafting, never Conversions. FromCrafting.Categories includes 'WoodPlanks', 'DecorativePlanks' and 'OrnatePlanks' - genuine native categories (every Wood_<Species>_{Planks,Decorative,Ornate}.json shares the same Wood_<Species>_Trunk ResourceTypeId input and the same 'Builders'/StructuralCrafting bench, only the recipe Category differs), so this is native-recipe composition, not invented content. The deriver surfaces 3 output categories per log species (33 conversions in all) and stamps each with its source category, so sneak+F offers 'Planks'/'Decorative'/'Ornate' for whatever log is loaded. A plain-F press with no picker selection defaults to the FIRST authored Categories entry, so the array order below (WoodPlanks first) is the default priority; reorder it to change that default, sneak+F still offers all three. Yield is purely DETERMINISTIC: Base 1 matches the native yield (every derived recipe in all three categories authors OutputQuantity 1 against a single-trunk Input, true across all 11 wood species), so reading it tells you exactly what one cycle makes. Everything conditional lives in Bonus, as visible Rolls whose Grants.OutputItems add whole EXTRA planks - additive, so the two numbers stay directly comparable and no file can silently multiply another's. The first Bonus roll is the tool ladder that pays for the milling time, so a starter hatchet earns nothing extra and every upgrade is felt. Its Factors sum THREE tool axes because no two of them can rank the vanilla hatchet ladder alone: quality (the native ItemQuality.QualityValue - Junk 0, Common 1, Uncommon 2, Rare 3, Epic 4, Legendary 5) at weight 10.0 dominates, item level at 0.1 breaks ties inside a quality tier, and gather power at 1.0 rewards the genuinely better cutter. Quality alone cannot separate Wood/Crude from Copper (all three are Common) and power alone cannot either (Wood and Copper share an identical 0.2 Woods power, and power SATURATES at 0.5 from the mid ladder up, flattening every top tier); item level separates them (4/4 vs 11) but must stay a small term, because it does not track rarity - Onyxium is Epic at item level 4, so a level-led formula would rank it below a copper hatchet. The resulting curve over the vanilla hatchets: Wood 10.6 and Crude 10.55 reach no floor (1 plank); Copper 11.3 reaches the 11 floor (2); Iron 22.3 reaches the 22 floor (2, plus the half below); Thorium 33.5, Cobalt 34.0 and Adamantite 34.5 reach the 33 floor (3); Onyxium 40.9 and Mithril 45.5 reach the 40 floor (4). Floors are NOT cumulative - the highest one reached wins, and two floors sharing a Min is a validator warning since only the last authored one could ever be reached. The second roll is Iron's half, now visible as its own band: it applies only at quality tier 2 and pays one more plank half the time, so Iron averages 2.5 rather than being rounded onto a neighbour and collapsing a rung. The third roll is the occasional windfall for everyone: a 2 percent base chance plus the held tool's gather power, capped at 25 percent, granting one extra plank when it wins. ContributionScale is the same ladder shape applied to the action's per-cycle contribution amounts - the engine pre-scales, so a listening mod grants the forwarded amount verbatim and cannot double-count. This jar's own action declares no PerCycleContributions at all (its content is progression-free by design), so the scale sits ready for whichever mod adds them and describes the same tool curve in one place. Every number here is a tunable leaf: reweight Factors to change what the curve rewards, move a floor Min to change which tier earns which step, or append a floor for a modded tier above Epic. A station deriving categories whose native recipes are NOT 1:1 should author Yield.Scale rather than Base, since the native quantity is not readable at the derivation seam. Worker and Moments below are this jar's own shipped standalone defaults, tuned in-game so the sawmill looks right with no pack installed: Puppet.Offset.Z 1.0 and Yaw 0.0 position the working puppet at the bench, Custody.Display.Offset.Y -0.1 embeds the placed log slightly into the bench top, and Work.CycleMs 4805 is the tuned cadence. The work animation rides the default Action-slot clip against the held hatchet's own animation set, with Swing.IntervalMs 933 driving the re-fire. An ExtensionAsset carries real Puppet/Custody/ContributionScale keys with per-leaf overlay semantics, so a pack re-skinning this action authors only the leaves it re-tunes and inherits the rest of these defaults.
